name: Cambridge Blue
lede: Cambridge blue is a pale, soft blue-green tied to the university and its boat-race colors.

sections.title: An Eton color on loan
sections.body:
Paterson calls Cambridge blue the light blue of Eton, adopted in the sixteenth century by Cambridge University [1][2]. A story says the shade was adopted in haste for the 1836 boat race, when the Cambridge cox had forgotten his crew's own colors [1]. Treat that as a story: Paterson himself says it is only "said" to be so [1].

The swatch here is greener than the sky blues around it, and its neighbors include [[eton-blue]], [[light-blue]] and [[oxford-blue]]. Eton blue and Cambridge blue are the same light blue in Paterson's account, so the college name rides on a school's older color [1][2]. Paterson's color index lists it among the blues, alongside Coventry blue and Devonshire blue [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color turns up in 0.53% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (127 paintings, as photographed) [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 3.0 times the rate expected from the museums' baseline [3].
